messages:
Alex P: Heads-up — we're prepping a new cloud account/project for eu12 to host the next GPU cluster. Sparse CIDR allocation from shared pool (only /20 available). Need a quick network scaffold and a handoff when ready.
Alex P: Requirements: 8x A100 (initial), private control-plane, centralized egress, no public IPs on worker nodes, service endpoints for metrics/logs, KMS for disk encryption.
Marie (netops): Thanks. Sparse CIDR means we can't create large subnet per AZ. Proposal: carve out 3x /26 subnets for control-plane, 6x /25 for nodes (auto-scale ranges), and reserve a /28 for NAT/infra. Thoughts?
Josh I: That sounds tight. Are we still using shared-services VPC for outbound or do we want dedicated NAT gateway in-region? Cost-wise central NAT via transit will be cheaper but adds hop/latency.
Priya S: For compliance, eu12 must have customer-managed KMS. Also tag policy: team:redwood-inference, env:staging|prod, cost-center:infra. Please include iam bindings in scaffold.
Alex P: Prefer using shared-services transit for now to avoid per-account egress costs; but we need an SR to ensure bandwidth/throughput for GPU artifact pulls (large docker layers). I'll open SR for transit capacity.
Marie (netops): OK. Two blocking items: 1) cloud provider only allows 64 concurrent public IPs by default in this org (so no worker public IPs), 2) GPU quota currently 0 in eu12. Put quota request ticket in parallel.
Alex P: Filed quota PR-4521 for 8 A100s and bootstrap IP waiver request (ticket NET-778). Linking here: https://internal/tickets/PR-4521 and NET-778.
Josh I: Terraform snippets for the scaffold — posting minimal example for the control-plane subnet allocation and route through transit:
```hcl
resource "azurerm_subnet" "control" {
  name                 = "rg-control-subnet"
  resource_group_name  = var.rg
  virtual_network_name = azurerm_virtual_network.vnet.name
  address_prefixes     = ["10.64.0.0/26"]
}
resource "azurerm_route_table" "rt-transit" {
  name                = "rt-transit"
  resource_group_name = var.rg
  route {
    name                   = "to-transit"
    address_prefix         = "0.0.0.0/0"
    next_hop_in_ip_address = var.transit_ip
  }
}
```
Marie (netops): Nice. Add a network policy to block worker->worker egress to internet and allow only registry/storage endpoints. Use service endpoints/private link where possible.
Priya S: Add KMS key ARN and rotation_policy in TF module. Also ensure logs go to central logging in shared-services with a retention tag (90d staging / 365d prod).
Alex P: Quick validation checklist before handoff: 1) VNet/subnets created, 2) route-table attached to subnets, 3) NAT path verified (curl to egress test URL), 4) KMS key available, 5) GPU quota approved, 6) TF state pushed to remote backend. Can someone run these and confirm?
infra-bot: Ticket PR-4521 status -> pending quota approval from provider. NET-778 -> pending network ops review.
Marie (netops): I'll run the scaffold apply tomorrow morning and do the NAT smoke (curl + large object download test). I'll post the apply log and a short sanity pass. Once NAT and subnets look good, @Josh I can start the cluster bootstrap.
Josh I: I'll queue the cluster bootstrap once Marie posts apply logs. Bootstrap steps I'll run: kubeadm-ish control-plane bring-up, attach node pools with gpu taints, verify kubelet node allocatable, then run a small perf job to validate GPU provisioning (tfbench).
Alex P: Thanks team. After the perf job and networking smoke we can handoff to oncall and mark the account as ready. Please add any post-handoff runbook notes in the ticket. :thumbsup:
__notes: Followed agents.md: single-string thread, messages prefixed with names, metadata fields only.
